examples/

Tracked, sanitized snapshots of validated scenarios and completed runs, copied out of the git-ignored workspace/ by scripts/snapshot_example.sh. Everything under examples/<scenario_id>/ is text, carries no credential, and is listed with a sha256 in that package's manifest.json; bash scripts/verify.sh 10 re-hashes every listed file, requires each to be tracked, and scans all tracked text for credential-like strings. A package is enough to read how a task was built, what the controls did, what an agent submitted, and why it earned the reward it did, without Modal, Docker, Temporal or the stakeholder service.

What an example contains

Path What it is Written by
manifest.json scenario_id, spec_hash, snapshot_at, files (package-relative path to sha256), skipped, the redaction and path-rewrite bookkeeping, a per-run summary the snapshot script
scenario.json the frozen scenario: source thread, persona, ledger facts with quoted spans and URLs, natural and withheld briefs, requirements and groups, checks, controls, environment. spec_hash is its content hash draft (model, code-validated)
assets/ oracle.diff, test.patch (the hidden FAIL_TO_PASS tests), plausible-wrong.diff, the three tamper diffs draft
approval.json which code-owned gates passed (approved_by: auto-validators means no human looked; review_needed stays true) approve
compile.json compiled_hash, pinned image_digest, run_config_hash, agent hosts, the three task directories compile
validation.json executed controls on Modal (nop, oracle, one plausible-wrong, three tamper), each with the full reward row and its expectation, plus the git-history probe; status: valid is what lets the scenario exist validate
scores.json per `condition brief_profile
task__full/, task__hidden/, task__interactive/ the Harbor 0.23 task directories: task.toml, instruction.md, environment/ (agent image, root-only collector, ask-user, confirm-behavior and request-review shims), tests/ (verifier image, test.sh, grader.py, policy.py, parsers.py, run_pytest.py, test.patch, grader_config.json), solution/, controls/ compile
runs/<trial_id>/record.json the ledger row: condition, profile, model, attempt, spec_hash, compiled_hash, run_config_hash, timings, reward, report, transcript run
runs/<trial_id>/reward.json the finite numbers the verifier wrote (reward, success, F2P and P2P counts, groups, integrity_signal_count, outcome_code, patch_applied) verifier
runs/<trial_id>/report.json the verifier report (per_test, per_group, applied_paths, dropped_paths, integrity_signals, regression, receipt, runner tail) plus the fields the run stage adds: transcript_binding_valid, simulator_validity, image_digest, harbor_exception, reviewed_equals_submitted verifier, then run
runs/<trial_id>/transcript.json the stakeholder's record of the interactive session (empty {} for full and hidden) the hosted stakeholder service
runs/<trial_id>/episode.json the export: policy_visible (instruction, agent trajectory, replies as the agent saw them), evaluator_only (report, ledger, author-only facts, test and oracle assets, audit), lineage (every hash), interaction, training_eligible export
runs/<trial_id>/agent/trajectory.json the agent's own record of its steps (ATIF, from mini-swe-agent through Harbor) the agent harness
runs/<trial_id>/verifier/ submission.diff, the raw report.json and reward.json, grader.log, runner_stdout.txt, test-stdout.txt as the verifier container wrote them verifier

Not included: the collected tree app.tar (about 6 MB per run), the raw mini-swe-agent.* logs, the per-trial task copy (it carries the session token), and run_config.json/spec.json (their hashes are in record.json, and the spec is scenario.json whenever record.spec_hash equals the package spec_hash, which the script enforces).

Sanitization is recorded, not assumed. manifest.redaction names the rules (SWESIM_SESSION_TOKEN values, Authorization and x-api-key header values, bearer tokens, and known credential values from the trial's task copy, the ignored env file and the environment) and lists files_changed; the replacement is always <redacted>. manifest.path_rewrites lists how absolute host paths were rewritten: to runs/<trial_id> or task__<condition> when the target is in the package, to a repo-relative workspace/... path when it is not.

The stakeholder host in compile.json and the three task.toml files is the placeholder example--swesim-stakeholder-web.modal.run, not the deployment that ran these trials. The manifest digests cover the files as tracked. The recorded compiled_hash was computed over the deployed host, so recompiling with your own stakeholder URL gives a different hash.

The included example: mwaskom--seaborn-3190 (version 2)

SWE-bench annotated instance mwaskom__seaborn-3190 (boolean data in a continuous color scale), rebuilt as version 2 on 2026-09-13 through CreateTasksWorkflow with --rebuild: spec 812be6e0..., compiled e208a80f..., image sha256:5ce876a5..., validated on Modal. validation.json shows the control table that admitted it: nop reward 0 (F2P 0 of 1, P2P 84 of 84, outcome 3), oracle reward 1 (outcome 1), one plausible-wrong control reward 0, each of the three tamper controls reward 0 with a protected-path-edit signal, and a probe that could not reach the gold commit from the shipped git object database. task__full/tests/grader_config.json has 85 expected ids (1 FAIL_TO_PASS, 84 PASS_TO_PASS) and one requirement group g01. Version 2 differs from version 1 in three ways: the stakeholder speaks as the reporter and answers confirm-behavior (the environment/shims/ directory now has three shims), the fact that described the regression test is author-only, and the withholding model selected no spans on this draft, so the scenario has only the natural brief (scenario.json → briefs). Version 1 is archived on the VM under workspace/scenarios/mwaskom--seaborn-3190/archive/v1/.

Three runs, all on the natural brief, all reward 1.0, chosen to show the v2 interaction:

  • runs/c1846a15feb5afc61bfdc76e/ is interactive, claude-sonnet-5: the agent asked one question that stated its intent (treat booleans as categorical or as 0/1 on a continuous scale?), the stakeholder answered in behavior ("False -> 0.0 and True -> 1.0 … should not fail"), the agent then ran confirm-behavior with a description of the fix and the stakeholder confirmed it with no unmet requirement. Patience 6 → 3. The transcript is frozen, its hash recomputes from events and equals report.receipt.transcript_hash (transcript_binding_valid true); every reply carries regenerated: false and an empty redacted_terms.
  • runs/dc88e7322955749303867fee/ is interactive, claude-haiku-4-5: one question with the same two options, the same behavior-level answer, one confirm-behavior, reward 1.0 with 85 of 85 tests passed.
  • runs/f9435904e9de18475cbd980e/ is hidden, claude-haiku-4-5: the same brief with no stakeholder, reward 1.0. It is the control for the two interactive runs; on this scenario the model does not need the stakeholder to pass.

training_eligible is false on the interactive runs because interactive episodes stay simulator_validity: unadjudicated until a person labels them. All three compiled_hash values match the package.

Reproducing the grading offline

Read, in this order, then recompute; nothing here needs a network.

  1. Integrity. Every file the manifest lists hashes to the recorded digest: 
    uv run --frozen python -c "
import hashlib, json, pathlib
root = pathlib.Path('examples/mwaskom--seaborn-3190'); m = json.load(open(root / 'manifest.json'))
bad = [p for p, h in m['files'].items() if hashlib.sha256((root / p).read_bytes()).hexdigest() != h]
print('ok' if not bad else bad)"
  2. What the contract was. task__<condition>/tests/grader_config.json: expected_tests maps every id to f2p or p2p, groups maps every FAIL_TO_PASS id to one weighted group, protected lists the paths a submission may not change (tests/test.patch is applied over them before running). instruction.md is what the agent saw.
  3. What was submitted. runs/<trial_id>/verifier/submission.diff is a unified diff the verifier regenerated from the pristine tree and the graded tree for report.applied_paths (dropped protected paths are not in it). report.submission_sha256 hashes the whole submitted change set and report.patch_sha256 the applied one; when they differ, dropped_paths says why.
  4. What the verifier observed. report.per_test gives expected and observed per id from the four-way evidence cross-check (collected ids, JUnit, terminal summary, exit code); per_group, regression, integrity_signals, receipt (collector status, tree hash, transcript hash) and runner_tail are there too.
  5. Recompute the reward from 2 and 4 and compare with reward.json: 
    uv run --frozen python -c "
import json
run = 'examples/mwaskom--seaborn-3190/runs/c1846a15feb5afc61bfdc76e'
rec = json.load(open(run + '/record.json')); rep = json.load(open(run + '/report.json'))
cfg = json.load(open('examples/mwaskom--seaborn-3190/task__%s/tests/grader_config.json' % rec['condition']))
observed = {t['id']: t['observed'] for t in rep['per_test']}
regression = any(observed.get(t) != 'passed' for t, k in cfg['expected_tests'].items() if k == 'p2p')
reward = sum(g['weight'] for g in cfg['groups'] if all(observed.get(t) == 'passed' for t in g['tests']))
reward = 0.0 if regression else min(1.0, round(reward, 8))
success = int(bool(observed) and all(v == 'passed' for v in observed.values()))
print(reward, success, json.load(open(run + '/reward.json')))"
    This is the rule in swesim/verifier/grader.py (and docs/grading.md): credit per requirement group, zero on any PASS_TO_PASS failure, success only when every expected id passed. reward is exported for training and for explaining near misses; success and outcome_code decide pass rates. Outcomes 3 to 7 (agent-invalid-submission, agent-runtime-failure, collection-failure, simulator-failure, evaluator-failure) never carry credit; 5 to 7 are infrastructure and leave the pass-rate denominator. A submission with nothing left after the path policy is outcome 3 regardless of what the tests would say.
  6. Optional re-execution, not offline: the task directories are complete Harbor tasks with a pinned image digest, so with Modal credentials uv run --frozen harbor run --max-retries 0 -p examples/mwaskom--seaborn-3190/task__full --agent oracle -e modal --yes rebuilds the images and must reproduce the oracle row of validation.json (--agent nop the nop row). Only Modal has been exercised. task__interactive needs a live stakeholder session and is run through swesim run, not harbor directly.

Two records of one episode

agent/trajectory.json is the agent's own account, written by the agent harness inside the sandbox: useful for reading what it tried, never an input to grading, and not protected against a policy that misreports. The verifier grades the collected tree, not the trajectory.

transcript.json is the stakeholder's account, written by the hosted service outside the sandbox: every question, review and reply with sequence numbers and patience, then a freeze. At the end of the agent phase the root-only collector archives the tree and, in the same hook, calls POST /freeze; the service seals the transcript, hashes its events (sha256 of the canonical JSON, sort_keys=True, separators , and :), and that hash is written into the collector receipt beside the tree hash. The run stage then fetches the transcript and sets report.transcript_binding_valid only if the session is frozen and the fetched hash equals the receipt's. Recheck it:

uv run --frozen python -c "
import hashlib, json
run = 'examples/mwaskom--seaborn-3190/runs/c1846a15feb5afc61bfdc76e'
t = json.load(open(run + '/transcript.json')); r = json.load(open(run + '/report.json'))
h = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(t['events'], sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')).encode()).hexdigest()
print(t['frozen'], h == t['transcript_hash'] == r['receipt']['transcript_hash'], r['transcript_binding_valid'])"

The snapshot script recomputes this for every copied transcript and refuses to write if it does not match; the manifest records transcript_hash_recomputed and transcript_modified_by_redaction per run. A redaction inside a transcript would break the hash, so it must never be needed: the session module that writes events (swesim/stakeholder/session.py) never handles the token, which the service checks and discards before the session sees a request.

Snapshotting another scenario

Preconditions: workspace/scenarios/<id>/validation.json says valid; compile.json matches the three workspace/tasks/<id>__* directories; each trial has record.json (status completed, same spec_hash), reward.json, report.json, transcript.json, its Harbor job directory still on disk, an export, and an entry in scores.json. Then:

SWESIM_WORKSPACE=$PWD/workspace uv run --frozen swesim score <scenario_id> --k 3
SWESIM_WORKSPACE=$PWD/workspace uv run --frozen swesim export <scenario_id>
bash scripts/snapshot_example.sh <scenario_id> <trial_id> [<trial_id>...]
bash scripts/verify.sh 10
git add examples && git commit

The script copies exactly the file set above, redacts before anything is written, rewrites host paths, refuses binary files (they cannot be scanned), skips runner_stdout.txt and test-stdout.txt over 200 KB and lists them under manifest.skipped with the source digest, writes the manifest, and finishes with an independent grep for credential-like strings that deletes the package on a hit. It never overwrites an existing examples/<id>/: remove it deliberately, or set SWESIM_EXAMPLES_DIR to write elsewhere. SWESIM_WORKSPACE and SWESIM_ENV_FILE are honoured as everywhere else. Keep a package near or under 5 MB; this one is 95 files and about 1.8 MB.
